title: Hybrid detection: fast single-candidate first, disambiguation second
trigger: Detecting a label from noisy input where a cheap deterministic stage resolves most cases and an expensive stage handles the rest
principle: Use a fast deterministic stage first — when it yields a single candidate, resolve immediately. Run the expensive probabilistic disambiguation stage only for ambiguous multi-candidate cases.

cases.context: Language detection from subtitle text — most scripts map to one language, but Latin/Cyrillic/Arabic need disambiguation
cases.bad:
// always run frequency profiles — slow + false positives on unambiguous scripts
const lang = frequencyDetector.detect(text); // 38 profiles for every input

cases.context: Fallback when no frequency profile meets threshold — must still return a sensible answer

applyFor: Spam filtering (rule-based first, ML model second only for ambiguous)
Type inference (literal type first, flow analysis second)
Any detection pipeline with cheap-then-expensive stages where most inputs resolve at stage 1
